note: Central ontological anchor; quotes FCM's third-form rooting-in-time claim verbatim, but never distinguishes it by name from forms I/II (FE).

Boredom glossed as 'a feeling of time' via FCM p.80, set against Kant's a priori inner sense and Augustine's Confessions XI; depth explicitly decoupled from clock-duration (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.309-310).

Horror vacui and nothingness-anthropologically-processed-as-death frame boredom's meaninglessness; Lipovetsky's 'living without purpose or meaning' extends the diagnosis into postmodernity (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.320).

Organizing move of the whole essay: resociologizes an apparently existential/trait-like attunement (profound boredom as fundamental attunement of Dasein) as leisure-economy-produced and situational, without abandoning its ontological register (FE).
'Boredom or fun' (Roma o morte) posits fun/entertainment as boredom's consumerist contrary pole, without invoking Csikszentmihalyi-style flow vocabulary (FE).
FCM's first-form vocabulary (drive-away/shake-off, Zeitvertreib, FCM pp.79/91) used generically for 'boredom' as such, unnamed as a distinct form (FE).

Zabalo's generic 'feeling of time' gloss (FCM p.80) and pastime/'drive away'-'shake off' vocabulary (FCM pp.79, 91) draw on fcm-04's own §20/§22/§23 material without distinguishing form I from the other forms (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.308-311).

Zabalo's rooting claim -- 'the more profound it becomes, the more completely boredom is rooted in time' -- quotes fcm-06 §1 verbatim; the essay's entire sociological extension is built on treating this third-form claim as boredom's general truth (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.309).

(P/anticipatory-application) Zabalo's whole 'free time'/spectacle-society question -- has leisure-economy man become boring to himself -- restates fcm-07's own question ('Has man in the end become boring to himself?', p.161) without citing its chapter-five locus; the cross-reference is ours, not Zabalo's own citation.

(P/anticipatory-application) Zabalo's 'gathering with loved ones but lonely, stuck to a screen' scene reads as an unnamed instance of fcm-05's surface-occupied/depth-hollow being-bored-with structure; Zabalo never names or cites the second form.
Primary interlocutor throughout; FCM, The Concept of Time (1924), Being and Time, and What is Metaphysics? all cited (FE).
Time as a priori form of inner sense, read alongside Heidegger's phenomenological time (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.309-310).
Confessions Book XI quoted via Heidegger's Concept of Time on disposition/measuring time (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.310).

The Principle of Hope cited on neoliberal management of leisure time ('invigoration', the 'dull and desperate stroll') (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.316-318).
The Society of the Spectacle cited on temps-marchandise / spectacular time (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.320).

Zabalo qualifies the standard Heidegger/Adorno antagonism narrative, arguing the 'few coincidences...are not casual, but rather rooted on a common ground' traceable to Nietzsche (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.313).

Article's core analytical move: resociologizes Heidegger's ostensibly trait-like fundamental-attunement account of profound boredom into a situational, leisure-economy-produced condition, without abandoning the ontological register (FE).
Zabalo's own coinage: reframes Garibaldi's motto as a consumerist alternative between (Rome=)fun and (death=)boredom (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.321).
(P/anticipatory-application) Extends profound boredom's ontological analysis into a socio-economic register (leisure industry, social media, spectacle culture) that FCM itself does not develop.
German pastime-term glossed etymologically and then illustrated sociologically via the vacation/leisure industry (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.311, 316).
Zabalo imports Debord's term to characterize commodified leisure time as boredom's evasion-vehicle (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.320).
Sloterdijk's metaphor (itself quoting Heidegger) for the privileged atmosphere in which boredom persists as 'a restless guest' (FAITHFUL-Zabalo, p.324).

Pastime/entertainment is diagnosed as symptomatic masking of boredom's disclosure rather than an adaptive, corrective regulatory response; no functional-account vocabulary is used (FE, qualified -- this is an absence/counter-reading this unit flags, not an explicit rebuttal of Elpidorou-style accounts, which Zabalo does not cite).

(P/anticipatory-application) OUR link: Zabalo's screen-mediated pastime-as-boredom-evasion account (smartphones, social media) offers a sociological vocabulary for reading Part III's VLE engagement/disengagement data as partly structurally produced rather than purely dispositional; not a claim Zabalo makes about students, VR, or education -- scale mismatch (societal vs. classroom) must be flagged whenever reused.
